solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Copper, mildly indecent, in church office

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
racy jokes are a little risqué

explanation.surface: A police officer telling slightly smutty stories while working in a church office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman, but it is the metal, whose chemical symbol is CU.
explanation.definitionFit: A curacy is the post held by a curate, an assistant clergyman's appointment within the Church.

clue.text: Long-legged insect big bird observed on rush

indicators.note: in a down clue, one thing sitting on another is written above it, so the first piece comes first

blocks.note: a crane is a tall wading bird
to fly is to rush or hurry

explanation.surface: Someone spots a gangly insect near a large bird perched on a reed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rush' suggests a reed the bird stands on, but it is the verb meaning hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: The crane fly, or daddy-long-legs, is a slender flying insect known for its very long, fragile legs.

clue.text: In Rhode Island differ about origin of literary competition

indicators.note: the origin of a word is where it starts, so only its opening letter is used
to be about something is to surround it, so one piece goes round another

blocks.note: RI is the US state abbreviation
things that differ vary
its first letter

explanation.surface: Writers in Rhode Island disagree over where some literary contest began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Rhode Island' looks like the setting of the scene; it actually supplies the opening letters, with 'In' just placing them.
explanation.definitionFit: Rivalry is the state of competing with someone, so the two nouns name the same contest between parties.

clue.text: Singer caught on time, one leaving Venetian island

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so that letter drops out of the word

blocks.note: c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time
the Rialto is the famous island district and bridge of Venice
the Roman numeral one, removed

explanation.surface: A singer was caught out on time as someone left the Venetian island.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rialto is the Venice district best known for its bridge over the Grand Canal; 'caught' uses the cricket scorecard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A contralto is a woman with the lowest female voice, so she is a particular kind of vocalist.

clue.text: Clear direction given twice for person with exclusive right

blocks.note: patent means obvious or clear
E for east, a compass direction, written two times

explanation.surface: Someone who owns an exclusive right is given the same clear instruction twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clear' sounds like a verb, but it is the adjective, as in a patent lie.
explanation.definitionFit: A patentee holds a patent, the legal grant giving sole rights to make or sell an invention.

clue.text: Doctor Wood supports a craving for a cut of beef

indicators.note: in a down clue, whatever supports sits underneath, so that piece is written last

blocks.note: taken as written
an itch is a restless longing
Bones, short for sawbones, is slang for a doctor
teak is a hardwood

explanation.surface: A doctor called Wood backs someone's hunger for a particular joint of beef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is usually an anagram signal or DR; here it is BONES, as in Star Trek's Dr McCoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Aitchbone is the rump bone of cattle, and steak cut from beside it is a named butcher's cut.

clue.text: Supporter, sly type, deserted by wife

indicators.note: being deserted means being left, so that letter is abandoned and taken out

blocks.note: a weasel is a sneaky, cunning person
w is the abbreviation for wife, removed

explanation.surface: A backer, a crafty sort, has been abandoned by his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the W from WEASEL.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a stand that holds up a painting or board, so it is literally a supporting frame.

clue.text: Asian giant importing British energy

indicators.note: to import is to bring something inside, so one piece takes in the others

blocks.note: the Titans were mythical giants
B is the abbreviation for British
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A huge Asian company brings in electricity from Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Asian giant' reads as a business, but the definition is just 'Asian'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tibetan is a native of Tibet, a region of Asia, so this names one particular kind of Asian person.

clue.text: Complete set of books embraced by European republic

indicators.note: whatever is embraced is held in arms, so it sits inside the other piece

blocks.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A full collection of books is welcomed by a European country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complete set' wants to be read together, but 'Complete' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Entire and complete are adjective synonyms describing something whole with nothing missing.

clue.text: Academic’s weakness initially leaving gold around part of church

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only a first letter is taken
being around something can mean close by it, so these letters are simply placed alongside

blocks.note: a vice is a moral failing
the chancel is the area around the altar
its first letter
or is heraldic gold

explanation.surface: A scholar's failing first shows when gold goes missing from the church.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking definition to wordplay; OR is the heraldic word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A vice-chancellor is the head of a British university, so the title names a senior academic.

clue.text: In a canine expert, see member of Christian group

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit inside it, so one letter goes within the other word

blocks.note: taken as written
canines are teeth, so a dentist is an expert on them
v stands for vide, Latin for see

explanation.surface: Inside a dog specialist's practice you meet a member of a religious sect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canine expert' suggests a vet, but canines are teeth. V for 'see' comes from the Latin vide used in references.
explanation.definitionFit: Adventists belong to Protestant churches, like the Seventh-day Adventists, that await Christ's Second Coming.

clue.text: Southern Italian explorer giving up cape for shoe

indicators.note: giving something up means surrendering it, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
John Cabot, born Giovanni Caboto, was an Italian navigator
C is the map abbreviation for cape, removed

explanation.surface: A southern Italian adventurer trades in his cloak for footwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cape' looks like a garment swapped for a shoe, but it is the geographical C.
explanation.definitionFit: A sabot is a wooden clog, the traditional carved footwear of French and Dutch peasants.

clue.text: General prepared to expatiate

indicators.note: what is prepared has been made ready or worked up, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An army general has got ready to speak at length.
explanation.walkthrough: To enlarge on a subject is to expand upon it at length, which is what expatiate means.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to speak or write about something more fully, adding detail and elaboration.

clue.text: Case of composer about to retire

indicators.note: to retire is to draw back, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: Gustav Holst wrote The Planets
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: The story of a composer who is about to give up work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to retire' reads as someone nearing retirement; the phrase actually splits, with 'to retire' acting on 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: A holster is a leather sheath for a pistol, so it is a fitted container for a gun.

clue.text: Constant horseplay oldies partially backed

indicators.note: partially means only in part, so just a stretch of the letters is used
something backed has moved in reverse, so the letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: the letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: Older people were partly supportive of endless rough-and-tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the end of horseplay and the start of oldies backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Constant here means faithful and steadfast, the same quality a loyal friend shows.

clue.text: Trick poet with writing fluid

blocks.note: Thomas Hood was an English poet
w is the abbreviation for with
ink is the liquid pens write with

explanation.surface: A prank played on a poet involving his ink.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Hood is a 19th-century English poet often used in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoodwink someone is to deceive or fool them, so both verbs mean to dupe.

clue.text: You and I grin broadly, imbibing wallop in tree?

indicators.note: imbibing is drinking in, so one piece takes another inside it

blocks.note: we covers you and I
to wallop is to hit hard
to beam is to smile widely

explanation.surface: Two people drinking beer up a tree, smiling from ear to ear.
explanation.walkthrough: Wallop is also British slang for beer, which is what 'imbibing' suggests; here it means a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: The whitebeam is a British deciduous tree whose leaves have pale, whitish undersides.

clue.text: Begged to figure among those looked for

blocks.note: to figure among a group is to be one of them
those looked for are sought

explanation.surface: Someone pleaded to be counted among the people being searched for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' suggests a number, but it means to appear or be present.
explanation.definitionFit: Besought is the old past tense of beseech, to implore or plead earnestly with someone.

clue.text: Cadge rugs, once refurbished

indicators.note: refurbished things are done up and remade, so these letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Begging for carpets that have already been restored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' looks like a time word but simply supplies four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To cadge is to get something by begging or sponging, which is exactly what scrounging means.

clue.text: Jumble left in small sailing boat

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit inside it, so one letter goes within the other word

blocks.note: a cutter is a small single-masted vessel
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A heap of junk abandoned in a little yacht.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' reads as abandoned, but it only supplies L.
explanation.definitionFit: A jumble is an untidy mixed heap, the same as clutter lying about a room.

clue.text: Woman originally involved with Descartes?

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so only the opening letter is used
with means alongside, so the two pieces are simply joined together

blocks.note: its first letter
the philosopher's first name was René

explanation.surface: Was a woman romantically linked with the philosopher Descartes?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the philosopher gives his first name, not his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene is a female given name, so it stands for a woman in the usual crossword way.

clue.text: Hurried over, primarily incensed about explicit art

indicators.note: to turn over is to flip upside down, so in a down clue the letters are reversed
primarily means first of all, so the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: to tear along is to hurry
its first letter
ca is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: Someone rushed across, furious about some pornographic artwork.
explanation.walkthrough: CA stands for circa, Latin for around, used before approximate dates.
explanation.definitionFit: Erotica means books, pictures or other works dealing with sexual desire, so it is sexually frank creative material.

clue.text: Raise castle’s running costs

blocks.note: to up something is to raise it
the keep is a castle's central tower

explanation.surface: Increase what it costs to maintain the castle.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Upkeep is the ongoing expense of maintaining property, the regular bills of running something.

clue.text: Feature of birds boy attendant spotted round Angus’s chimney

indicators.note: going round something encircles it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: a page is a young attendant
lum is Scots for chimney; Angus is a typically Scottish name

explanation.surface: Birds nesting around a Scotsman's chimney were seen by a pageboy.
explanation.walkthrough: The name Angus signals that the word is Scottish.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumage is a bird's covering of feathers, the characteristic trait that marks out birds.

clue.text: Porter, possibly, carrying very soft fruit

indicators.note: whatever carries something holds it inside, so one piece contains another

blocks.note: porter is a kind of dark beer
pp, pianissimo, is the musical direction for very soft

explanation.surface: A railway porter is carrying some very squashy fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' suggests a luggage carrier, but it is the dark beer, one example of ale.
explanation.definitionFit: An apple is a common orchard fruit, so it is a specific example of the general category.

clue.text: Draw game? He painted frescoes

blocks.note: a tie is a drawn match
polo is a game played on horseback

explanation.surface: Sketching a game, and a question about who painted murals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' suggests painting, fitting the frescoes, but it is a tied result.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Battista Tiepolo was an 18th-century Venetian painter famed for vast ceiling frescoes.

clue.text: Broadcast poets preclude by legal rule

indicators.note: to broadcast is to scatter widely, so these letters are strewn into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Poets on air are barred by a point of law.
explanation.walkthrough: Estop is a legal term; the related noun estoppel is better known.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, to estop a party is to bar them from asserting something contrary to an earlier position.

clue.text: Inclination to adopt very English raising agent

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so one piece is placed inside another

blocks.note: a leaning is a tendency
v is the abbreviation for very
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A tendency to take up a particularly English way of baking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raising' suggests bringing up children to adopt, but it is bread rising.
explanation.definitionFit: Leavening is yeast or baking powder that makes dough rise, so it is the substance that lifts bread.

clue.text: Split up before crossing river for formal flower garden

indicators.note: crossing something means straddling it, so one piece spans another

blocks.note: to part is to separate
ere is poetic for before
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A couple separate before crossing the river to reach a formal garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' reads as a time word joining clauses; it supplies ERE.
explanation.definitionFit: A parterre is an ornamental garden of flower beds laid out in a symmetrical pattern.

clue.text: Impression made by this writer’s agreement

blocks.note: this writer is the setter, I, and I'm is I am
a pact is an agreement

explanation.surface: A lasting effect produced by the author's contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This writer's' means I'M, the setter speaking of himself with 's for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An impression is the effect something has on people, just as an impact is a strong influence.
